soft_rejections.D: Highest upfront cost is a real issue for a small office budget. Also, no espresso or milk drinks means we lose options for people who want more than basic filter coffee.

already_said: Dedica fits the counter space and budget perfectly, plus it makes solid espresso for the team that wants quality coffee. The slow throughput worries me, though—ten people might get impatient.
We need to remember Dedica demands more hands-on use—it’s not just slow, it means someone’s stuck making drinks one by one while others wait. That’s a real bottleneck for ten people.
You get great espresso with Dedica but it’s a slow drip for ten people. Ninja handles volume with ease but eats up counter space. We pick speed or size—can’t have both.
Eva, Dedica’s fine if you’re cool with everyone waiting and juggling cups, but how much hands-on time can we actually afford during busy mornings?
Waiting and juggling cups is a real bottleneck no matter how many espresso lovers we have. Dedica’s compact size wins here, but can we handle the slowdown without chaos?
The Ninja’s big 12-cup capacity really moves the needle for me, especially at that price. Still like Dedica’s espresso quality and small footprint, but that slowdown is a bigger deal now.
Just to be clear, Ninja’s bigger footprint won’t fit well on our small counter. That’s a real tradeoff to weigh.
We don’t know who needs espresso here, but speed and volume matter more with ten users. Ninja’s capacity beats all, so if espresso lovers are few, it’s the smarter pick despite the size.
We don’t know if there’s flexible space, but if we can’t rearrange, Ninja’s size will cramp us. That means we might have to prioritize counter space over capacity.

Moccamaster makes 10 cups at once, just two less than Ninja’s 12. So if size’s tight, Moccamaster still covers most of our volume needs. But Ninja’s price and capacity combo is hard to beat if we can carve out space.
I'd go with Ninja.
Highest upfront cost is a real issue for a small office budget. Also, no espresso or milk drinks means we lose options for people who want more than basic filter coffee.
I still like Ninja for capacity and price, but the smaller counter means Moccamaster works better here—my pick is Moccamaster.
Might be worth the Ninja despite the bigger footprint, given the 12-cup capacity.
Maybe better to take Ninja for volume and price, even if it’s a bit bigger.
Maybe it could work if espresso lovers are few, but we don’t know that here; slower pace might still annoy most.
I still like Ninja, but I’ll go with Moccamaster for its reliable 10-cup capacity.

already_said: I like how Senseo handles both pads and filter coffee without busting our budget, though I wonder about how well it holds up day to day.

Today we're deciding: Choose a coffee machine for a small shared office kitchen.
For this simulated decision, I’ll treat the following setup as the shared facts.
Options:
A) Moccamaster KBG Select — cost: 299 euros; capacity: 10 cups; type: filter (+ reliable for shared pots; − no espresso or milk drinks)
B) DeLonghi Dedica — cost: 179 euros; capacity: single shots; type: espresso (+ compact and good for espresso; − slower for many users)
C) Philips Senseo Switch — cost: 119 euros; capacity: 7 cups; type: pads and filter (+ flexible and cheap; − pad waste and weaker taste)
D) Ninja Filter Brewer — cost: 149 euros; capacity: 12 cups; type: filter (+ large capacity for the price; − larger footprint)
Context: The maximum budget is 320 euros.; The kitchen counter is small.; About ten people use the machine on office days.
Which machine is the best fit for price, reliability, maintenance, and daily throughput?
